texts.setting.instructions_per_frame.about: How many CHIP-8 instructions the machine runs in one frame: its speed. 0 uses the variant's own speed, or the speed Cadmium knows for the program (15 for the first CHIP-8, 30 for SUPER-CHIP, 1000 for XO-CHIP). A program that runs too slowly or too fast for you can be given another number. The "vip", "cosmac-vip", "dream-6800" and "chip-8-strict" variants keep their own time and ignore this. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.random_seed.about: The number the machine's random numbers start from. A real machine starts from whatever happens to be there; with this number fixed, the same project always plays the same way, and another number gives a program another run of luck. The "vip", "cosmac-vip", "dream-6800" and "chip-8-strict" variants make their random numbers themselves and ignore this. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.variant.about: Which CHIP-8 machine runs the program. There are many kinds of CHIP-8, and a program written for one often misbehaves on another. "auto" lets Cadmium decide: it knows many programs by their contents, and otherwise goes by the file's extension (.ch8, .sc8 for SUPER-CHIP, .xo8 for XO-CHIP, .mc8 for MegaChip, and so on). Choose one yourself when a program runs wrongly, or when its file has no extension Cadmium knows. The "vip" variants, "cosmac-vip" and the "dream-6800" ones emulate the whole original computer running its own CHIP-8 interpreter, which is slower and the most faithful, and can run programs that contain machine code. "chip-8-strict" has the original COSMAC VIP's exact timing without emulating the computer. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.slot.program.help: The CHIP-8 program. Its extension says which kind of CHIP-8 it is for: .ch8 (the kind is worked out from the program), .sc8 SUPER-CHIP, .xo8 XO-CHIP, .mc8 MegaChip, .ch10 CHIP-10, .c8x CHIP-8X, .c8e CHIP-8E, .hc8 a program with COSMAC VIP machine code in it, .c8tp the VIP's 64x64 mode, .c8b a file holding versions for several kinds. An Octo cartridge (.gif) and an Octo source file (.8o) are compiled when the project starts; a source file that includes other files is not supported. A .bin, .ram or .vip file is loaded into a bare COSMAC VIP with no CHIP-8. Nothing else is needed: the machines' own programs are part of Cadmium.
